text:
lee_support: ping — customer_acme reporting 401s across a batch of ingestion jobs right after we rotated their API key in Vault. customer saw ~30% of requests failing with 401, same endpoints that were fine before rotation.
customer_acme: confirmed we rotated the key at 10:12 UTC via our tooling. Some worker logs show Authorization failed (401) with X-Request-ID: rq_8f3a. We kept the old key for 5 minutes then revoked.
lee_support: do we know if their workers pick up env changes or use a sidecar?
customer_acme: they use a sidecar that writes REDWOOD_API_KEY to /etc/envvars and processes read from there at boot. We thought sidecar would roll refresh automatically.
ops_maya: hunch — sidecar probably updated file but long-lived processes keep the old in memory. Also possible CDN or reverse proxy cached header-based auth. Quick checks: inspect pod env var and vault-agent logs.
samir_eng: can you paste a short snippet of the failing request/response headers (mask the key)? even just the first 8 chars helps. Also check the vault rewrap logs for errors.
customer_acme: snippet: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
X-Request-ID: rq_8f3a
Response: 401 Unauthorized
```
lee_support: thanks. Ask them to run these in the cluster and paste outputs:
```
kubectl exec -it <pod> -- cat /etc/envvars | grep REDWOOD_API_KEY
kubectl logs -l app=sidecar -c vault-agent --tail=200
kubectl get pods -l app=worker -o wide
```
customer_acme: ran the first command, shows old key prefix (abcd1234) in /etc/envvars. sidecar logs show successful write at 10:12 but the worker pod started at 09:50 and hasn't been restarted.
ops_maya: there it is — long-lived process won't re-read file. Either restart the worker deployment or trigger a HUP that your runtime honors. On k8s easiest is: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/worker`.
samir_eng: additional note — if you have any edge auth caches (CDN or API gateway) those can cache a token->allow decision for a short TTL; recommend purge/flush or wait TTL. Also double-check Vault TTL/lease: if the sidecar fetched a wrapped value with a short lease and rewrap failed it could revert.
customer_acme: we restarted worker pods, errors dropped to 0% within a minute. Thanks. Couple follow-ups: could we make sidecar send a graceful reload signal to the app or have the app watch file changes?
lee_support: good to hear. For the short term doc: sidecar writes + long-lived process = restart required unless the app supports SIGHUP or watches files. Recommend adding a watcher or for k8s use an annotated rollout on secret change.
samir_eng: internal action item — add a note to the docs about "Secrets written to disk require process reload" and a k8s rollout example. Also add a troubleshooting snippet for identifying cached auth at the edge (how to test with curl bypassing CDN).
deploy-bot: reminder: created ticket ENG-1278 to add a k8s secret-rollout example to the support playbook.
customer_acme: one more oddity — one of our lambdas (cold start) picked up the new key immediately while long-running ones didn't. Makes sense now. thanks :thumbsup:
lee_support: marking resolved for now, will follow up once ENG-1278 has a doc. If the customer wants, we can run a helper script to detect any pods still holding the old key.
ops_maya: snippet to detect pods with old prefix: `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- sh -c "grep -R \"abcd1234\" /proc/*/environ || true"` (may need permissions).
samir_eng: also check for any in-memory caches or SDKs that do token pooling. We should add guidance for library-level refresh handlers.
lee_support: noted. closing thread — thanks everyone :white_check_mark:
